* Collaborate with ML Researchers, Technical Artists and Simulation engineers to bring new ML techniques to our production simulator

* Improve rendering and tooling for generating realistic data at scale

* 3+ years of experience with Python/C++ programming and algorithm design
* Experience building and extending radiance field ML models

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
As a Machine Learning Engineer at Zeromatter, you'll be at the forefront of creating the neural backbone that powers next-generation autonomous systems. You'll develop cutting-edge ML models that transform simulation fidelity, behavior prediction, and robotic learning capabilities. This role offers the rare opportunity to apply state-of-the-art machine learning techniques to solve real-world robotics challenges while working with a team that's redefining what's possible in simulation technology.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Develop and implement machine learning models to improve the realism of simulated sensor data, including for example approximation of light transport, material models, 3D representation and black box sensor characterization.
* Develop content generation systems for creating diverse and realistic simulation scenarios, including for example, perception signals from geospatial data, measurements from novel hardware, and both structured and unstructured text conditioning.
* Create behavior models for various actors in our simulations (e.g., pedestrians, vehicles, drones).
* Design and implement reinforcement learning algorithms for training robotic systems within our simulation environment.
* Optimize ML model performance for simulation applications, including low latency inference, architectural improvements and model compression.
* Collaborate with the software engineering team to integrate ML models into our core simulation platform.
* Work with customers to understand their ML-related needs and develop tailored solutions.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Master's or PhD in a relevant field (e.g. computer science, mechanical engineering, physics, math, robotics, etc.) or equivalent working experience.
* Strong programming skills in Python and experience with ML frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
* Deep understanding of machine learning architecture and algorithms, particularly those applicable to robotics and simulation (e.g., computer vision, reinforcement learning, generative models).
* Experience applying ML techniques to real-world problems, preferably in robotics, autonomous systems, or simulation; including building and maintaining data pipelines and datasets.
* Familiarity with software engineering best practices, including version control, testing, and CI/CD.
* Bonus: Experience with systems programming languages such as C, C++ and Rust (with Rust preferred)
* Bonus: Experience with low-level GPU programming, such as CUDA or Vulkan.
* Bonus: Experience with distributed computing for large-scale ML training.
* Bonus: Familiarity with ML model deployment and serving in production environments.

Compensation Range: $100K - $300K

The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (www.bosch.com), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. The Research and Technology Center North America (RTC-NA) is dedicated to providing technologies and system solutions for various Bosch business fields, primarily in the field of artificial intelligence, energy technologies, internet technologies, circuit design, semiconductors and wireless, as well as advanced MEMS design.

As a part of the global research, our AI research in Silicon Valley focuses on Foundation Models, Explainable AI (XAI), Agentic AI, Computer Vision, Data-driven Robotics, Data Science, AI System Engineering, Time-series Analysis. Engineers today are building some of the most ambitious machines humanity has ever seen. They should have AI that’s purpose-built for them.

Hardware engineering teams use Nominal to simulate, test, manufacture, and operate the physical systems that keep the world moving, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation energy systems and robotics.

We’re looking for engineers who want to take on hard problems and help make a new generation of world-changing hardware possible.

  
  

### **About Hardware Intelligence**

  
  

We're going after the biggest opportunities to accelerate how the world engineers: agents that are expert at engineering physical systems, not just competent at calling tools. Nobody has a recipe for that yet. Hardware gives us an edge most domains lack: real test results to check agent work against. * Find where our agents fail on real hardware work, from customer traces and from tasks you design with hardware experts.

jobs.description:
Overview:

Founded in 1921, the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is a leading nonprofit membership organization, research center, and publisher, with headquarters in New York, an office in Washington, DC, and programs nationwide. It is dedicated to increasing America's understanding of the world and contributing ideas to U.S. foreign policy. CFR’s 5,000+ members are leaders in international affairs and foreign policy. CFR also publishes Foreign Affairs, the preeminent magazine on global issues, and provides up-to-date information about the world and U.S. foreign policy on its award-winning website, CFR.org.

Position Summary:

The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is seeking an experienced DevOps engineer / Site Reliability Engineer. This role is responsible for maintaining the secure and reliable functioning of our digital properties including CFR.org, ForeignAffairs.com, Think Global Health, The China Open Source Observatory, and other associated web and mobile sites. The portfolio spans a managed WordPress VIP publishing platform, Pantheon publishing platform, and custom AWS applications.

This role owns the reliability, resilience, security, and observability of those properties, the delivery pipeline that ships to them, and a growing set of AI and agentic services built on top of them. Your goal is to prevent outages; when incidents happen, you lead the response and make sure we learn from them. You will work closely with the software engineering team and report to the associate vice president of product, design, and engineering.

This full-time position is based in CFR’s New York City or Washington D.C. office on a hybrid basis. CFR currently defines hybrid status as working at least four days a week onsite, with Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite.

Essential Functions/Responsibilities:

* Define and track SLOs and error budgets for each property. Own on-call, incident response, root cause analysis, and blameless postmortems.
* Run observability, logging, and alerting systems (Datadog, Dash0) to track service health, improve resilience, and prevent downtime, and raise issues before visitors or stakeholders ever see a problem.
* Own infrastructure, backup, and disaster recovery documentation and execution.
* Maintain the CI/CD pipelines for CFR.org and our applications, including WordPress VIP and Pantheon deploys as well as custom AWS apps; debug failed runs and keep configurations current.
* Provision and manage AWS infrastructure as code with Terraform, with policy checks and drift detection in the pipeline.
* Identify opportunities to use automation, testing, and deployments.
* Build security into every stage of delivery: manage Okta-based role-based access, own secrets, key management and rotation.
* Own infrastructure, backup, and disaster recovery documentation and execution.
* Own AWS security posture and edge/WAF configuration.
* Lead incident response, determine root cause on production issues, mitigate, and provide technical support to the engineering team as needed.
* Assist DevSecOps contractors, vendors, and cross-functional technical contributors to deliver against the platform roadmap

Minimum Qualifications:

**Experience**

* 3-7 years experience in DevOps, SRE, platform or security engineering.
* Proven experience with AWS and infrastructure as code with Terraform.
* Experience with managed platforms such as WordPress VIP, Pantheon, Acquia, or similar.
* Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines with automated testing and multi-environment deployments. Familiarity with supply-chain security tooling.
* Hands-on experience applying zero-trust principles. SSO/MFA through an identity provider (Okta), least-privilege IAM, short-lived credentials, and secrets management (1password, AWS Secrets Manager or similar).
* Scripting in Bash and Python. Working familiarity with PHP and Node.js/TypeScript. Working knowledge of WAF/CDN services such as Cloudflare, Cloudfront, or, Fastly.
* Strong communication and problem solving skills, serving as a collaborative bridge across engineering, operations, IT, and vendors.

Required Application Materials:

Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position.

Compensation and Benefits:

* The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $150,000 – $175,000, depending on experience.
* In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs.

About CFR:

The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations.

jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Your best work shouldn't be hidden behind your last employer's name.**  
  
Some of the strongest engineers we've worked with wouldn't stand out in a resume stack. They didn't all come from FAANG. They didn't all have CS degrees from the usual schools. Some did, some didn't, and it made less difference than you'd think.

What made them stand out: hand them an ambiguous problem and an unfamiliar codebase, and they shipped something real. Quickly.

They read the code before asking for help. They picked up new tools without being told to. They weren't thrown by systems they didn't understand on day one. And they built things that held up in production.  
  
**That's who we're looking for.**  
  
**The opportunity**

Peri is recruiting Software Engineers, including founding and early backend roles, for some of New York's most compelling AI startups, from Seed to Series D+, backed by investors including a16z, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Notable Capital, and Thrive.

We've worked closely with the founders, studied the engineers who thrive on their teams, and learned what really sets them apart.

The short version: **Ownership, speed, technical judgment, and the ability to learn fast often count for more than the name at the top of your last offer letter.**

You don't need to have worked on AI products already. If you have, great. If you haven't, keep reading.  
  
**What you'll actually do**

Imagine joining a team where the product is still taking shape.

There's no thick onboarding doc. The architecture has decisions you'd make differently. The roadmap changes when a customer says something surprising.

Your job is to make it work. Understand what users actually need. Make the tradeoffs. Design the system, write the code, ship it, and fix it when real traffic finds what tests didn't.

You're part builder, part architect, part problem-solver.

You'll work directly with founders. You'll own features and systems end to end, not just tickets. And you'll see your work in front of customers within days, not quarters.

These roles are for engineers who like having the whole problem.  
  
**Who we're looking for**

Maybe you're an engineer at a big company who keeps wanting to touch more of the stack than your team allows.

Maybe you taught yourself, switched careers, or grew into responsibilities long before anyone gave you the title for them.

**We take all of that seriously.**

But here's the thing.

**We need you to show us.**

A resume won't tell us how you debug something you've never seen, how you make decisions with incomplete information, or what you do when the obvious approach falls over.

So walk us through it.

Tell us about a system you designed. A bug that took you days to track down. A technology you had to master in a week. Something you built that nobody asked you to build.

It doesn't need to be impressive-sounding. It needs to be real.  
  
**Why aren't the companies listed?**

Because this isn't one opening.

We work with several teams looking for similar engineers, each building something different.

Rather than you running six interview loops in parallel, we'd like to understand how you think and what you're great at, then point you toward the teams where you'd fit best.

We only work with companies we'd be excited to join ourselves.  
  
**Who is Peri?**

Most technical recruiting is keyword matching: languages, frameworks, years of experience, last employer.

We think that leaves a lot of great engineers on the table.

So we start from the other end. We learn from founders what actually makes an engineer succeed on their team, then look for those qualities in people whose resumes may undersell them.

We're most interested in engineers who are better than their credentials suggest.  
  
**How to apply**

* Apply here or DM me on LinkedIn.
* We do want one answer: **What's the hardest or most interesting thing you've built, and what about it makes you think you're capable of more than your resume shows?**

  + A few sentences is enough. A link to code or a project is even better. Specifics beat buzzwords.
  + If there's a fit, we'll talk, share what we know about each team, and help you figure out which roles make sense. When there's a strong match, we'll connect you directly with the founders.

**And if you've ever thought, "I'm a much better engineer than my resume makes me look," we especially want to hear from you.**  
  
**One last thing**

Looking past credentials doesn't mean looking past ability.

If you're mass-applying without reading the post, can't show real engineering work, have a fabricated or misleading LinkedIn profile, or aren't authorized to work in the United States, please don't apply.

**It's not a good use of anyone's time.**

We'll overlook a pedigree. We won't overlook a lack of effort, skill, or honesty.  
  
**Show us what you've shipped, not what you say you can ship.**

Compensation Range: $150K - $350K

new_jobs.description:
Overview:

Founded in 1921, the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is a leading nonprofit membership organization, research center, and publisher, with headquarters in New York, an office in Washington, DC, and programs nationwide. It is dedicated to increasing America's understanding of the world and contributing ideas to U.S. foreign policy. CFR’s 5,000+ members are leaders in international affairs and foreign policy. CFR also publishes Foreign Affairs, the preeminent magazine on global issues, and provides up-to-date information about the world and U.S. foreign policy on its award-winning website, CFR.org.

Position Summary:

The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is seeking an experienced DevOps engineer / Site Reliability Engineer. This role is responsible for maintaining the secure and reliable functioning of our digital properties including CFR.org, ForeignAffairs.com, Think Global Health, The China Open Source Observatory, and other associated web and mobile sites. The portfolio spans a managed WordPress VIP publishing platform, Pantheon publishing platform, and custom AWS applications.

This role owns the reliability, resilience, security, and observability of those properties, the delivery pipeline that ships to them, and a growing set of AI and agentic services built on top of them. Your goal is to prevent outages; when incidents happen, you lead the response and make sure we learn from them. You will work closely with the software engineering team and report to the associate vice president of product, design, and engineering.

This full-time position is based in CFR’s New York City or Washington D.C. office on a hybrid basis. CFR currently defines hybrid status as working at least four days a week onsite, with Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite.

Essential Functions/Responsibilities:

* Define and track SLOs and error budgets for each property. Own on-call, incident response, root cause analysis, and blameless postmortems.
* Run observability, logging, and alerting systems (Datadog, Dash0) to track service health, improve resilience, and prevent downtime, and raise issues before visitors or stakeholders ever see a problem.
* Own infrastructure, backup, and disaster recovery documentation and execution.
* Maintain the CI/CD pipelines for CFR.org and our applications, including WordPress VIP and Pantheon deploys as well as custom AWS apps; debug failed runs and keep configurations current.
* Provision and manage AWS infrastructure as code with Terraform, with policy checks and drift detection in the pipeline.
* Identify opportunities to use automation, testing, and deployments.
* Build security into every stage of delivery: manage Okta-based role-based access, own secrets, key management and rotation.
* Own infrastructure, backup, and disaster recovery documentation and execution.
* Own AWS security posture and edge/WAF configuration.
* Lead incident response, determine root cause on production issues, mitigate, and provide technical support to the engineering team as needed.
* Assist DevSecOps contractors, vendors, and cross-functional technical contributors to deliver against the platform roadmap

Minimum Qualifications:

**Experience**

* 3-7 years experience in DevOps, SRE, platform or security engineering.
* Proven experience with AWS and infrastructure as code with Terraform.
* Experience with managed platforms such as WordPress VIP, Pantheon, Acquia, or similar.
* Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines with automated testing and multi-environment deployments. Familiarity with supply-chain security tooling.
* Hands-on experience applying zero-trust principles. SSO/MFA through an identity provider (Okta), least-privilege IAM, short-lived credentials, and secrets management (1password, AWS Secrets Manager or similar).
* Scripting in Bash and Python. Working familiarity with PHP and Node.js/TypeScript. Working knowledge of WAF/CDN services such as Cloudflare, Cloudfront, or, Fastly.
* Strong communication and problem solving skills, serving as a collaborative bridge across engineering, operations, IT, and vendors.

Required Application Materials:

Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position.

Compensation and Benefits:

* The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $150,000 – $175,000, depending on experience.
* In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs.

About CFR:

The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations.
